bull_bear.body: Debt reduction priority: Working capital debt (~INR 115cr) expected to be paid down over next 4 years as capex slows and cash generation improves; Finance costs targeted to approach zero; Capital subsidies received/utilized (INR 7cr total for Chandipur, ~INR 10cr expected for Sanand).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Persistent raw material inflation; Prolonged export weakness in US/EU due to tariffs and lack of FTAs; Delay in passing on price hikes to customers; Global supply chain shifts favoring competitors like China in specific markets.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasizes resilience and long-term structural domestic growth despite short-term export volatility; Confident in 10-12% growth floor; Focused on margin recovery to historical 14-15% levels once input costs stabilize.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Argentina market reopening due to government change boosted LatAm exports; Unorganized sector attrition due to compliance costs is a silent growth driver; Distributors stocking up ahead of price hikes creates short-term demand spikes; TAA (Trade Agreements Act) list exclusion limits US government procurement opportunities for India.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net Debt to Equity (x) is shown as 0.25 (FY24), 0.37 (FY25) and 0.37 (FY26).
- Net Worth (INR Mn) is shown as 2,375 (FY24), 2,986 (FY25) and 3,184 (FY26); equity share capital is flat at INR 62 Mn across FY24-FY26 with no minority interest.
- Balance sheet borrowings are predominantly short term: Short-Term Borrowings INR 890 Mn (FY24), 1,133 Mn (FY25), 1,141 Mn (FY26) against Long Term Borrowings of INR 37 Mn, 25 Mn and 62 Mn respectively.
- The deck makes no statement on dividend policy, buybacks, or a stated capital-allocation philosophy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- integration: Integrated head-to-toe PPE portfolio lets customers source multiple safety solutions from a single partner — evidence: company describes itself as offering 'one of India's most comprehensive portfolios of head-to-toe personal protective equipment'.
- customer lock-in: High repeat business gives revenue visibility and lowers customer-acquisition needs — evidence: more than 90% of orders came from repeat customers in FY25-26.
- distribution: Established global distribution network across many countries — evidence: exports to more than 55 countries across six continents, served through an international distribution network and 80+ dealers across 15 countries.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Intense competitive environment — Competition from global brands, low-cost manufacturers and regional players may exert pressure on pricing and market share; the PPE industry is becoming increasingly competitive, reducing product differentiation.
- Foreign exchange and geopolitical risk / export market concentration — Export-oriented operations remain exposed to currency fluctuations, trade policy changes and geopolitical uncertainties; Europe, the company's most significant export geography, contributed approximately 75% of export revenues and remained burdened by subdued industrial activity; the US faced tariff-related disruptions.
- Regulatory and certification requirements — Evolving international safety standards and certification norms require continuous investment in compliance and product development.
- Reputation and product quality / liability risk — As a manufacturer of safety-critical products, any product quality issue, recall or compliance lapse could adversely impact customer trust, brand reputation and result in financial liabilities.
- Supply chain disruption — Dependence on raw material suppliers and global logistics exposes operations to procurement delays, cost inflation and supply disruptions.
- Working capital intensity — Maintaining a broad product portfolio and servicing institutional customers requires significant inventory and receivables, increasing working capital requirements.
- Regulatory and export policy changes — Changes in export incentives, customs duties, product standards or international compliance requirements could affect profitability and market access.
- High dependence on industrial demand cycles — Revenue remains closely linked to sectors such as manufacturing, construction, mining and oil and gas, making performance sensitive to industrial investment cycles.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Domestic business grew ~20% YoY acting as primary growth engine; Exports faced headwinds due to US tariffs and EU demand slump; New categories (PU Coated Gloves, PVC Gumboots) launched for import substitution; Sanand unit running at ~50% capacity targeting INR 40cr annual revenue potential.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Describes itself as the "Largest integrated Indian Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) manufacturer" with "one of the widest protective gear product range catering to diversified industries", offering a one-stop solution from helmets, eyewear, ear protection, face masks and safety garments to gloves and safety shoes.
- Claims deep customer stickiness with "over 90% of orders coming from repeat customers", and describes itself as an ISO certified and government registered trading house.
- Positions as "one of the largest exporters of PPE products from India exporting to 55+ countries across 6 continents"; Q1-FY27 geographical revenue mix is Asia 62%, Europe 22%, Americas 15%, Australia 1%, Africa 0%.
- Claims to be "one of the few companies to have an indigenous expertise with various raw materials such as textile, leather, rubber, and plastic", built over three decades, and "the leading safety shoe manufacturer and distributor from India".
- Cites experienced management with over 40 years of industry experience and dedicated R&D centres and teams for product innovation and improvements.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Distribution] The 'SMILE' reseller programme "received an overwhelming market response, expanding the distribution network to over 1,000 resellers across India".
- [Domestic traction] "Achieved the highest-ever Q1 domestic revenue despite a volatile pricing environment, reflecting strong market execution."
- [Supply chain] Seaport congestion delayed procurement of critical raw materials and customer deliveries in Q1-FY27.
- [Shareholding] As on 30th June, 2026: Promoter 73.68%, Public 26.32%.
- [Authorship] The presentation was prepared by Valorem Advisors, an independent investor-relations management service company, which certifies its directors/employees own no stock in the company.

business.body: Mallcom manufactures and exports personal protective equipment across hand, head, face, respiratory, body and foot protection categories, serving customers through globally certified manufacturing facilities and in-house testing laboratories. It sells to industries including manufacturing, construction, infrastructure, mining, engineering, energy, logistics and healthcare, with exports to more than 55 countries across six continents.

business.body:
- **Hand protection:** Leather hand gloves, Seamless knitted gloves, NBR-coated gauntlet gloves, PU-coated gloves, Cut-resistant, abrasion-resistant, impact-resistant and chemical-resistant gloves
- **Head protection:** Industrial safety helmets, Bump caps, Coral Bump Cap (EN 812:2012 certified)
- **Foot protection:** Safety shoes, Steel-capped safety shoes, Leather shoe uppers, PVC gumboots
- **Body protection:** Industrial work garments, High-visibility jackets, Rainwear, Protective aprons, Disposable coveralls, Flame-retardant fabrics and jackets
- **Respiratory protection:** Industrial masks and respiratory protection solutions
- **Face/eye protection:** Protective eyewear, Splash-resistant goggles, Face protection systems

latest_quarter.body: Q4/FY26 margins pressured by higher petro-based raw material costs (textiles, leather, polymers), freight, and energy; Lower sales realization in OEM export markets due to weak demand; Employee expenses increased due to scaling manpower for new facilities; Pricing power limited in commoditized export segments but stronger in branded domestic segment.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Minimum 10-12% for FY27; Margin: Targeting return to pre-investment normalized levels of 14-15%; Order Inflow: Stronger domestic traction expected; Capex: INR 10-15cr annually for FY27 onwards (maintenance + incremental lines).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Domestic demand driving growth; Export orders constrained by US tariff barriers and EU weak demand; New PU Gloves and PVC Gumboots lines ramping up to address INR 80-90cr import market.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Import substitution in gloves/boots (INR 80-90cr addressable); Market share gain from unorganized sector due to labor code formalization and BIS strictness; Expansion in Middle East/Africa via new dedicated marketing arm; Potential US market recovery pending trade deals.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Expand across underpenetrated domestic markets and high-potential export regions, supported by the distribution network and differentiated portfolio.
- Strengthen the distribution ecosystem, expand brand visibility and deepen customer engagement across domestic and international markets.
- Leverage product innovation, channel partnerships and digital outreach to enhance market penetration and customer acquisition.
- Build a future-ready workforce by combining internal career development with targeted external recruitment; strengthen succession planning and technical/leadership capabilities.
- Deepen engagement with credible CSR partners and strengthen programmes delivering measurable, long-term community outcomes across road safety, education, community infrastructure and social welfare.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY25-26, Mallcom completed a major manufacturing expansion cycle: the Protec workwear facility at Sanand (Ahmedabad) commenced commercial production, the industrial safety footwear facility at Chandipur became fully operational, and the company began manufacturing PU-coated gloves and PVC gumboots (categories previously substantially imported into India). The Sanand facility was sited close to raw-material suppliers and an experienced glove-manufacturing workforce to strengthen supply-chain coordination and reduce procurement lead times. Management stated the year marked completion of a major investment cycle, with the financial priority now shifting from creating capacity to increasing utilisation of the Sanand and Chandipur facilities and improving returns on capital employed. Mallcom also established a marketing arm in the UAE during the year to support geographic diversification into the Middle East and Africa.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The workplace safety industry is expected to benefit from increasing regulatory focus, growing industrial activity and rising awareness of employee well-being across sectors, creating opportunities for organised, quality-focused PPE manufacturers.
- Demand remained broad-based across infrastructure, construction, manufacturing, engineering, automotive and logistics, with growing opportunities in Tier-II and Tier-III markets.
- International demand for certified, high-performance PPE reinforced the company's position as a trusted global manufacturing partner (export momentum driver).
- India's real GDP grew 7.7% in FY25-26 versus 7.1% in FY24-25, driven by strong consumption and increasing investment, supporting industrial activity and demand for occupational safety products.
- Manufacturing and construction growth of 7.1% within a secondary sector that grew 9.1% supported employment, industrial activity and demand for occupational safety products.
- Union Budget FY27 income-tax relief measures are expected to support discretionary consumption; continued infrastructure, manufacturing, MSME, skilling and innovation expenditure will strengthen industrial activity and employment generation.
- Improved liquidity and banking-sector asset quality, plus GST rationalisation, expected to strengthen domestic demand and business confidence.
- The World Bank projected India economic growth of approximately 6.6% for FY26-27.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Mallcom completed its ambitious capex cycle with new Sanand and Chandipur units now operational, positioning for volume-led domestic growth and import substitution despite Q4 margin compression from raw material inflation and weak export realizations. While FY26 PAT was distorted by a prior-year land sale gain, the core business is pivoting to capture market share from unorganized players driven by stricter labor codes and BIS norms.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Mallcom (India) Limited, established in 1983, is one of India's leading manufacturers and exporters of personal protective equipment (PPE), offering comprehensive head-to-toe safety solutions.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Mallcom manufactures and exports personal protective equipment across hand, head, face, respiratory, body and foot protection categories, serving customers through globally certified manufacturing facilities and in-house testing laboratories. It sells to industries including manufacturing, construction, infrastructure, mining, engineering, energy, logistics and healthcare, with exports to more than 55 countries across six continents.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Domestic business grew ~20% YoY acting as primary growth engine; Exports faced headwinds due to US tariffs and EU demand slump; New categories (PU Coated Gloves, PVC Gumboots) launched for import substitution; Sanand unit running at ~50% capacity targeting INR 40cr annual revenue potential.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Hand protection:** Leather hand gloves, Seamless knitted gloves, NBR-coated gauntlet gloves, PU-coated gloves, Cut-resistant, abrasion-resistant, impact-resistant and chemical-resistant gloves
- **Head protection:** Industrial safety helmets, Bump caps, Coral Bump Cap (EN 812:2012 certified)
- **Foot protection:** Safety shoes, Steel-capped safety shoes, Leather shoe uppers, PVC gumboots
- **Body protection:** Industrial work garments, High-visibility jackets, Rainwear, Protective aprons, Disposable coveralls, Flame-retardant fabrics and jackets
- **Respiratory protection:** Industrial masks and respiratory protection solutions
- **Face/eye protection:** Protective eyewear, Splash-resistant goggles, Face protection systems

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Domestic demand driving growth; Export orders constrained by US tariff barriers and EU weak demand; New PU Gloves and PVC Gumboots lines ramping up to address INR 80-90cr import market.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Minimum 10-12% for FY27; Margin: Targeting return to pre-investment normalized levels of 14-15%; Order Inflow: Stronger domestic traction expected; Capex: INR 10-15cr annually for FY27 onwards (maintenance + incremental lines).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Import substitution in gloves/boots (INR 80-90cr addressable); Market share gain from unorganized sector due to labor code formalization and BIS strictness; Expansion in Middle East/Africa via new dedicated marketing arm; Potential US market recovery pending trade deals.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The workplace safety industry is expected to benefit from increasing regulatory focus, growing industrial activity and rising awareness of employee well-being across sectors, creating opportunities for organised, quality-focused PPE manufacturers.
- Demand remained broad-based across infrastructure, construction, manufacturing, engineering, automotive and logistics, with growing opportunities in Tier-II and Tier-III markets.
- International demand for certified, high-performance PPE reinforced the company's position as a trusted global manufacturing partner (export momentum driver).
- India's real GDP grew 7.7% in FY25-26 versus 7.1% in FY24-25, driven by strong consumption and increasing investment, supporting industrial activity and demand for occupational safety products.
- Manufacturing and construction growth of 7.1% within a secondary sector that grew 9.1% supported employment, industrial activity and demand for occupational safety products.
- Union Budget FY27 income-tax relief measures are expected to support discretionary consumption; continued infrastructure, manufacturing, MSME, skilling and innovation expenditure will strengthen industrial activity and employment generation.
- Improved liquidity and banking-sector asset quality, plus GST rationalisation, expected to strengthen domestic demand and business confidence.
- The World Bank projected India economic growth of approximately 6.6% for FY26-27.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q4/FY26 margins pressured by higher petro-based raw material costs (textiles, leather, polymers), freight, and energy; Lower sales realization in OEM export markets due to weak demand; Employee expenses increased due to scaling manpower for new facilities; Pricing power limited in commoditized export segments but stronger in branded domestic segment.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Debt reduction priority: Working capital debt (~INR 115cr) expected to be paid down over next 4 years as capex slows and cash generation improves; Finance costs targeted to approach zero; Capital subsidies received/utilized (INR 7cr total for Chandipur, ~INR 10cr expected for Sanand).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY25-26, Mallcom completed a major manufacturing expansion cycle: the Protec workwear facility at Sanand (Ahmedabad) commenced commercial production, the industrial safety footwear facility at Chandipur became fully operational, and the company began manufacturing PU-coated gloves and PVC gumboots (categories previously substantially imported into India). The Sanand facility was sited close to raw-material suppliers and an experienced glove-manufacturing workforce to strengthen supply-chain coordination and reduce procurement lead times. Management stated the year marked completion of a major investment cycle, with the financial priority now shifting from creating capacity to increasing utilisation of the Sanand and Chandipur facilities and improving returns on capital employed. Mallcom also established a marketing arm in the UAE during the year to support geographic diversification into the Middle East and Africa.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasizes resilience and long-term structural domestic growth despite short-term export volatility; Confident in 10-12% growth floor; Focused on margin recovery to historical 14-15% levels once input costs stabilize.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- integration: Integrated head-to-toe PPE portfolio lets customers source multiple safety solutions from a single partner — evidence: company describes itself as offering 'one of India's most comprehensive portfolios of head-to-toe personal protective equipment'.
- customer lock-in: High repeat business gives revenue visibility and lowers customer-acquisition needs — evidence: more than 90% of orders came from repeat customers in FY25-26.
- distribution: Established global distribution network across many countries — evidence: exports to more than 55 countries across six continents, served through an international distribution network and 80+ dealers across 15 countries.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Persistent raw material inflation; Prolonged export weakness in US/EU due to tariffs and lack of FTAs; Delay in passing on price hikes to customers; Global supply chain shifts favoring competitors like China in specific markets.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Argentina market reopening due to government change boosted LatAm exports; Unorganized sector attrition due to compliance costs is a silent growth driver; Distributors stocking up ahead of price hikes creates short-term demand spikes; TAA (Trade Agreements Act) list exclusion limits US government procurement opportunities for India.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Expand across underpenetrated domestic markets and high-potential export regions, supported by the distribution network and differentiated portfolio.
- Strengthen the distribution ecosystem, expand brand visibility and deepen customer engagement across domestic and international markets.
- Leverage product innovation, channel partnerships and digital outreach to enhance market penetration and customer acquisition.
- Build a future-ready workforce by combining internal career development with targeted external recruitment; strengthen succession planning and technical/leadership capabilities.
- Deepen …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Distribution] The 'SMILE' reseller programme "received an overwhelming market response, expanding the distribution network to over 1,000 resellers across India".
- [Domestic traction] "Achieved the highest-ever Q1 domestic revenue despite a volatile pricing environment, reflecting strong market execution."
- [Supply chain] Seaport congestion delayed procurement of critical raw materials and customer deliveries in Q1-FY27.
- [Shareholding] As on 30th June, 2026: Promoter 73.68%, Public 26.32%.
- [Authorship] The presentation was prepared by Valorem Advisors, an independent investor-relations management service company, which certifies its directors/employees own no stock in the company.
